content: 1. Are windows designed to provide adequate ventilation and maintain habitable conditions? 2. Are reflective white roofs installed to reduce heat impacts? 3. Are pavements and roofs designed to withstand extreme temperatures or solar radiation? 4. Is there a mechanism in place to filter indoor and ambient air pollutants? 5. Is there a system for cooling the environment? 6. Are vulnerabilities identified to implement actions that reduce impacts? 7. Is there a strategy to stimulate increased water intake by staff and patients? 8. Does the healthcare facility have a syndromic surveillance system for drought-related illnesses? 9. Have capacities, resources, and needs been identified to better cope with and manage a drought event? 10. Are drought-resilient trees and plants present around the facility? 11. Is there an information system for tracking and monitoring diseases following drought events? 12. Are there procedures for procuring, transporting, and safely storing water supplies? 13. Are trees and leafy plants near windows used to provide natural cooling? 14. Is the health workforce equipped with a plan to identify and protect workers at risk of heat stress? 15. Are staff provided with a cool space or shower room? 16. Are staff trained on public health and climate change hazards, including health impacts related to heatwaves? 17. Are staff trained to manage hazardous waste (chemical, biological, radiological)? 18. Are staff aware of the need for an alternative action plan for outdoor functions, such as limiting activity during the hottest parts of the day or alternating work and rest periods in cooler areas? 19. Are staff aware of the types of patients and symptoms expected during a heatwave? 20. Is the health workforce informed on how to use and follow a surveillance system to track health outcomes? 21. Are staff aware of the need to stay hydrated and wear appropriate clothing? 22. Are windows exposed to the sun kept closed during the day and opened at night when temperatures drop? 23. Are curtains that receive morning or afternoon sun closed? 24. Are nonessential lights and electrical equipment that generate heat turned off? 25. Are there cool rooms or electric fans available for relief if temperatures are below 35°C? 26. Is there a quality monitoring plan for water intended for human consumption? 27. Is there a water management plan to identify water contamination? 28. Is there onsite water purification equipment to provide safe drinking water? 29. Is drinking water kept cool or refrigerated for staff, patients, and visitors? 30. Is water storage protected from direct sunlight? 31. Are water storage tanks equipped with appropriate covers to protect from excessive heat? 32. Is healthcare waste stored away from excessive heat in cool and covered spaces? 33. Are there collaborations with water utility agencies to prevent suspension of services? 34. Is there a water safety plan in place in case of water contamination? 35. Is there a cross-sectoral water management plan to conserve and protect local or alternative water sources? 36. Are heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems regularly assessed? 37. Is renewable energy (e.g., solar) sufficient to power critical equipment? 38. Are appliance thermometers in refrigerators and freezers used to ensure food, vaccines, and other essential refrigeration-dependent medical supplies are safe? 39. Is there adequate daylight to ensure proper visibility during power outages? 40. Is there clear guidance on heat-risk management for maintaining critical infrastructure (e.g., air conditioning, medical devices, computers, diagnostic equipment, boiling water)? 41. Is there a plan or regulation to determine ways to reduce overall energy use? 42. Are there collaborations with energy utility agencies to prevent suspension of electricity services? 43. Is there a management plan for intermittent energy supplies or system failure? 44. Are walls and roofs insulated? 45. Are there preparedness and training programs for periods of extreme heat? 46. Are reflective white roofs installed to reduce heat impacts? 47. Are green roofs installed to mitigate heat impacts? 48. Are pavements and roofs designed to withstand extreme temperatures or solar radiation? 49. Are light-colored pavements used in parking areas and walkways around the facility? 50. Is there a system for cooling the environment? 51. Are extra medical supplies available in case of increased demand for treatment of heat stress? 52. Is there a strategy to stimulate increased water intake by staff and patients? 53. Are loft and cavity walls insulated? 54. Is there a syndromic surveillance system for heat-related illnesses? 55. Is there a long-term strategy for reducing heat, such as through building insulation? 56. Is there an information system for tracking and monitoring diseases following heatwave events?
